newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-BUGEL NAMED RAIDERS' HEAD COACH.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-BUGEL NAMED RAIDERS' HEAD COACH.

text.p: Joe Bugel, the Oakland Raiders' offensive coach the last two years and former Arizona Cardinals' coach, was named head coach of the team, owner Al Davis said on Thursday.
Bugel, 20-44 with the Cardinals, replaces Mike White, who was fired December 24th after he guided the Raiders to disappointing 8-8 and 7-9 seasons in two years as coach.
"Approximately two weeks later (after the firing), I interviewed Joe Bugel as a potential head coach," Davis said. "I told Joe Bugel at that time, quite frankly, that he was the number-one candidate.

"While this was going on over the last four weeks, there was overwhelming support from our players relative to the hiring of Joe Bugel," Davis said. "There were trips to my office from players that I have not seen in my office in at least a year."
Davis' statements contradicted a report in Thursday's San Francisco Chronicle, which said Davis was hoping to entice old friend Bill Parcells from the New England Patriots.

But NFL commissioner Paul Tagliabue ruled that Parcells is contractually bound to the Patriots for the 1997 season and the report indicated Davis would be unwilling to provide the compensation sought by Patriots owner Bob Kraft.
"We want to really try to build that bridge between the past and our present," Bugel said. "Past Raiders laid a great foundation, laid a great tradition"
Bugel also thanked the players who spoke in favour of his hiring and said that kinship will translate into success.

"I'm not ashamed to tell our current football players I love them. I respect them," Bugel said. "I think that's the reason we will win not only one Super Bowl, but Super Bowls, in the future. The time is now."
